first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, so simplifying onboarding is the most directly aligned intervention for sustainable improvement. I will verify the prior onboarding and activation results before committing, while avoiding promotional pricing because its prior acquisition lift came with materially worse 30-day retention. A small guarded test limits downside and preserves the option to expand based on qualified activation and retention signals.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding simplification experiment. The verified result directly addresses the current completion decline and showed strong downstream outcomes: completion +13%, time-to-value reduced by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. Measure qualified activation, time-to-value, conversion, and 30-day retention—not completion alone—to ensure the lift produces sustainable revenue. Do not use promotional pricing, given its prior retention harm.

final2.rationale: Stay with the committed onboarding simplification experiment rather than pivoting mid-cycle to promotional pricing. The verified onboarding result directly addresses the current completion decline and improved 30-day retention by 3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. The deeper competitor discount increases pressure on price-sensitive SMBs, but promotional pricing previously harmed 30-day retention and should not be adopted without fresh evidence. Monitor SMB segment churn, qualified activation, conversion, and retention in the experiment; reassess pricing next cycle when verification is available.
